summary: This spec describes how the Tutor opens a conversation when a new source (today a repository, later Markdown, PDF or slides) arrives. A single arrival event leads to a Tutor-written opening question with topic rows. The opening is saved in the chat thread so a reload does not write it again.

options.label: One event for any source
options.what: You will see how one arrival event with the same shape serves every kind of source, and what a repository sends when its reading finishes.

options.label: How the Tutor writes the opening
options.what: You will see how a server action turns the source's summary and options into two or three short sentences ending in a question, with no repository read.

options.label: Opening joins the chat thread
options.what: You will see how the opening and its option rows become one Tutor message, how a fixed sentence covers a failed call, and when a new opening is written.

options.label: The Run it option and flag
options.what: You will see how a feature flag, off by default, decides whether the rows offer running the source first.

options.label: Saving and restoring openings
options.what: You will see how each opening is stored as a Tutor entry so a reload restores it without asking the model again.

options.label: What the tests check
options.what: You will see which behaviours the tests pin down: asked once, no extra rows on re-render, failure fallback, and the exact prompt.

cannot.thing: The actual code behind the mechanism
cannot.why: The document only describes the design and names the files, and it includes no code.

cannot.thing: The full wording of the opening prompt
cannot.why: Only a summary of the prompt is given, and the exact sentence is in a separate file.

cannot.thing: Handling of Markdown, PDF or slides sources
cannot.why: The document says only the event's shape is built now and the other kinds come later.
